newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Lower figure in EU budget pact not agreed - source.
newsitem.headline: Lower figure in EU budget pact not agreed - source.

text.p: European Union leaders still face a question of principle on Friday when they try to put the finishing touches to plans for a stability pact partially agreed by finance ministers earlier, a senior delegation source said.

Ministers agreed on the broad architecture of the stability pact but left it to government leaders to settle figures defining the exceptional circumstances which would exempt countries from fines if they ran up deficits over three percent of gross domestic product after the launch of monetary union.
A draft document suggested countries would be automatically exempt from fines if their economies had shrunk by 1.5 percent, though officials said a figure of 2.0 percent was also being discussed.
Below this level, EU ministers would decide whether a country could be exempt from fines even if their recession had not been so bad.
According to the draft document, "as a rule this provision will only apply in respect of an annual fall of real GDP of at least (0.75 percent)". The figure in brackets has not yet been agreed.
The delegation source said there was no agreement yet that there should be a figure at all setting this lower figure.
"There is no agreement that it should not be set at zero," he said.
This was the key reason why ministers had asked EU leaders to try to agree on the upper and lower figures on Friday.
"Behind the second (lower) figure there is a question of principle," he said.
